recipes.name: Easy Crescent Taco Bake
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can Pillsbury® refrigerated crescent dinner rolls
0.75 cup Old El Paso® Thick 'n Chunky salsa
2 tablespoons Old El Paso® taco seasoning mix (from 1-oz package)

steps.text: Heat oven to 375 degrees F. Unroll dough; separate into 8 triangles. Place in ungreased 9-inch square pan or 10-inch pie plate; press over bottom and up sides to form crust.

In 10-inch skillet, cook beef over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thoroughly cooked; drain. Stir in salsa and taco seasoning mix; simmer 5 minutes. Spoon meat mixture in crust-lined pan; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until crust is deep golden brown and cheese is melted. Served topped with lettuce and tomato.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Crescent Taco Bake
raw_recipe.description: Refrigerated crescent dinner rolls unite as a quick crust to hold ground beef, cheese, salsa and seasoning in this easy-to-assemble main dish.

review.reviewBody: This is an excellent recipe from Pillsbury. This was amazingly easy and so good. We love sour cream, so we had that with it. I would just caution to watch the baking time. Cresent rolls generally don't need that long to back. My crust was golden brown after 17 minutes, so keep an eye on it after it's been in the oven for 15 minutes and use your best judgement.

This was great. I used Newman's brand salsa which I find not as spicy, which I like. I did bake the crescent roll first for 9 minutes, filled with the filling and then cook an additional 8-9 minutes. I highly recommend doing this so you don't get a doughy crust. If you want the cheese melted without being hard put it on a few minutes before taking out of oven otherwise it makes a hard cheese crust on top, which I liked.

This was a huge hit with my wife! I used green chili’s instead of the salsa and used tapitio crumbled Doritos instead and baked for 18 minutes! Added sour cream and lettuce with sliced jalapeños on top! Thanks for the recipe!

Tried this last night for the first time...and will make it again! I personally don't care for written reviews of a recipe when the author lists dozens of changes and/or substitutions and then gives the recipe a poor review. That said, I will list a couple of deviations from the original recipe I made last night. First, I used the Crescent Dough Sheet (instead of the rolls) and pressed it lightly into a 9" x 13" casserole dish. Second, we love cheese in this house, so I increased the cheese (to about double) to fit our preferences. It was absolutely delicious...my 90-year old mother had seconds!

I started with salsa chicken in the crock pot. At dinner time, I made the crescent roll pie shell then scooped the chicken and cooked as directed. Unfortunately I let my avocado go bad so we topped with lettuce, tomatoes and black olives. Everyone liked it but I thought the crescent rolls added a sweetness to it that I didn't care for but not enough to stop me from getting seconds. This would be a really quick meal and a change from the norm for a weekday meal. I'll make again. I'm sure my oldest will request it.
I added crushed taco flavor Doritos before putting on the cheese, and covered with foil for the last 10 minutes. Whole thing was gone! Everyone loved it!

I had a tube of crescent rolls to use and had everything else on hand in the pantry. This was surprisingly easy and delicious. I used ground angus beef and added half a can of re-fried beans to the mixture, this added some body, along with the taco seasoning and salsa. Cheddar cheese melted beautifully. I topped with shredded lettuce, sour cream, diced tomatoes and slices of avocado. It was a hit. Easy to prepare and very satisfying.

This was a great, easy recipe. I made a few changes to it by adding onions and red peppers to the beef. Once done, I added taco sauce instead of salsa, a package of taco seasoning and one can of refried beans. I divided the croissant roll in half and layed both pieces in a 9 x 13 pan. Topped it with the beef/bean mixture and then the cheese. Served it with sour cream once out of the oven. This was a hit.

Great starter recipe. I added some kidney beans to the bottom before meat mixture. Added a can of diced tomatoes with green chiles instead of salsa. And cut up one onion with ground turkey instead of the beef. I baked at 350 for 20 minutes and came out perfect. Thanks for the recipe.
I cooked the crust for about eight minutes and kept an eye on it before adding the rest of the ingredients. Crust was perfect.

This recipe is very good, I however made just a few small additions. I added about 1/2 cup sour cream, shredded lettuce, grape or Cherry tomatoes(halved) & sliced black olives to the top when it comes out of the oven. Awesome!!!
Super easy and instead of the crescent rolls I used the Pillsbury dough that is a roll with no perforations.
It’s become a favourite dish in our household. My boyfriend loves it and asks at least once a week for it. Delightfully fast and easy to cook. Super tasty.
Really good. I added black beans and corn. Couldn’t be easier!
I did not have a tomato to garnish on top but this was a hot. It was easy, delicious and gone quick!
Great recipe! Simple, delicious, and easily customizable. It's a wonderful option when you're tired of regular tacos.

I made this tonight and it was so good! I didn't have a deep enough pan so I used a shallow casserole dish. I also added sliced black olives and chopped fresh cilantro to the topping and my boyfriend loved it! Thanks for an easy recipe!?

I have made this a couple of times and it never disappoints. I do agree that the time is a little long. I left mine in for 15 minutes, and then kept checking it. It was done in about 18 minutes. I just kept checking the crust until it looked right.
Will definitely make this again! Easy and delicious!
Quick, easy week night dinner. A new favorite at our house!
